page: Microsoft Azure M48bs_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processor operating at 4.0 GHz, offering 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 24 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor features 105 MB of L3 cache alongside support for advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). System memory totals 384.0 GB, establishing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-dense compute tasks. The instance does not include local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent computational and memory subsystem throughput. The virtual machine achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 19356.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 60379.92, driven by high vector and integer throughput. Memory subsystem tests demonstrated large-block uncached read bandwidth of 214.82 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 94.29 GB/sec, placing it within the upper performance tiers for memory streaming. In workload-specific tests, the instance recorded 24056.12 on PassMark database operations, 60.49 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, and 69.92 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The primary tradeoff of the M48bs_v3 is its reliance entirely on external block storage for persistent data, which requires careful provisioning of remote storage throughput. In qualitative terms, the instance offers balanced resource allocation for scale-up architectures requiring substantial memory density without paying for dedicated graphics hardware. Best-fit deployments include enterprise relational databases, in-memory caches, large software compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive ETL workloads.
